title: 一日百円です  (One Hundred Yen a Day)

segments.t: Outside Nakai's mansion, Ono bursts out laughing—the last salesman who visited that house ended up in the hospital! Fired up by his breakthrough, Muranishi develops his own passionate style, turning a three-thousand-yen monthly fee into a hundred yen a day. Listen to Muranishi find his voice.
やるじゃないか！
知ってたなら教えてくださいよ！
愛情だよ。一人前のセールスマンになれる。
英会話の必要性を感じますか？
俺には必要ないね。
わたくしはそのようには考えません。
一日十五分、三か月続けてみてください。
あなた様に人生を諦めてほしくないのです。
でもさ、少し高くない？
確かに少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
月三千円ということは一日百円です。
高いどころか安すぎると思っております。
Watch how Muranishi agrees politely with a customer's objection before flipping the price upside down.
やるじゃないか！
"'Well, look at you go!' Literally " We can hear
やるじゃないか
asks 'do you not do well?', an idiomatic pat on the back meaning 'hey, not bad at all!'
知ってたなら教えてくださいよ！
'If you knew, you should have told me!'  In this sentence,
知ってたなら
this word means 'if you knew', followed by
教えてくださいよ
, 'please tell me!' with an exasperated
よ
一人前のセールスマンになれる。
'You can become a full-fledged salesman.'  You can catch
一人前
literally counts 'one full person's portion'—used in sushi shops for one serving and at work for a professional who stands on their own feet.
俺には必要ないね。
"'I do not need it.' Adding " Focus on
には
onto casual
俺
, me, draws a line: 'as for me, there is no need',
必要ない
一日十五分、三か月続けてみてください。
'Please try keeping at it fifteen minutes a day for three months.'  Watch for
一日十五分
sets the pace at fifteen minutes per day, and
続けてみてください
attaches
みて
, try and see, to the verb for to continue.
あなた様に人生を諦めてほしくないのです。
'I do not want you to give up on your life.'  In this sentence,
人生
this word means a human lifetime, and the verb for to give up is used. Gluing
ほしくない
onto
諦めて
expresses 'I want you not to give up'.
でもさ、少し高くない？
"'Still, is it not a little expensive?' Customers everywhere ask " The character says
少し高くない
with a rising lilt—turning the word for expensive negative to nudge 'a bit pricey, right?'
確かに少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
"'Certainly, it might feel a little expensive.' Never argue head-on: Muranishi opens with " Watch for
確かに
, certainly, and cushions the thought with
かもしれません
, 'it might be'.
月三千円ということは一日百円です。
'Three thousand yen a month means one hundred yen a day.'  Listen for
月三千円
is three thousand yen a month;
ということは
bridges neatly into what that really means—
一日百円
, a hundred yen a day!
高いどころか安すぎると思っております。
"'Far from being expensive, I believe it is way too cheap.' Placing " The phrase contains
どころか
right after
高い
flips the claim completely—'far from expensive!'—and lands on
安すぎる
, and this word is built from the word for cheap, plus the word for too much. Now let's listen to Muranishi's price-flipping pitch again.
やるじゃないか！
知ってたなら教えてくださいよ！
愛情だよ。一人前のセールスマンになれる。
英会話の必要性を感じますか？
俺には必要ないね。
わたくしはそのようには考えません。
一日十五分、三か月続けてみてください。
あなた様に人生を諦めてほしくないのです。
でもさ、少し高くない？
確かに少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
月三千円ということは一日百円です。
高いどころか安すぎると思っております。
Remember the word for expensive, the word for cheap, the expression to invite someone to try something, and the bridging phrase whenever you reframe numbers in your favour. See you in scene sixteen.
さようなら。
